headline.purpose: Section titles, group titles, the house strip title.

title.purpose: Prices, cart heading, wordmark, the home h1 "What do you own?" at 700 in the picker bar, the promo offer line from 1024px at 400, filter sheet heading, empty-state title, desktop results count, home "Featured in" subheads.

body-small.purpose: Tile descriptions, tile facet lines, the picker guess line, trust row items at 600, breadcrumbs, filter and applied chips.

label.purpose: Tags, counts, scale marks, meta, segments, chip-group labels, category counts; at 400 the tile brand line and category blurbs.

figure-tile.purpose: Watt number beside the mini battery on product tiles; 1.5rem below 720px.

figure-pdp.purpose: Watt number inside the battery glyph on the house strip and product pages.

price-big.purpose: Product page price, with a 1.25rem muted strike-through.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: Cart drawer, the phone filter sheet and the row scroll buttons over a row edge; dropped when the filter sheet settles into the desktop rail.

shadows.name: suggested-ring
shadows.purpose: Second pixel of the suggested chip's green ring.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Dialog backdrop behind the cart drawer and the phone filter sheet.

motion.name: ease-charge
motion.purpose: House ease for fills, chip state, button press, tile rise.

motion.name: fill-battery
motion.purpose: Battery glyph fill, and the cart thank-you mini battery filling once from 0 to 100%.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Watt figure counting to its value.

motion.name: bolt-in
motion.purpose: Bolt appears after the fill starts.

motion.name: tile-rise
motion.purpose: Tiles entering grids; scroll-row tiles do not rise.

motion.name: sheet-up
motion.purpose: Phone filter sheet and the phone cart drawer opening (drawer-in-y).

motion.name: drawer-in
motion.purpose: Cart drawer opening from the right edge, 720px and up (drawer-in-x).

motion.name: shop-tile-rise
motion.purpose: Tiles re-rendering after a filter change on the category page.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: Skeleton tile blocks before data loads.

motion.name: promo-slide
motion.value: scroll-snap; scrollTo smooth (auto under reduced motion); dot fill 0.2s
motion.purpose: Promo card paging by swipe, prev/next, dots or arrow keys. No autoplay.

motion.name: payoff-into-view
motion.value: window.scrollTo smooth to the element top under the header, 12px clear (auto under reduced motion)
motion.purpose: Phones below 1024px: after a device tap on home, the payoff tiles, or the open model question, scroll under the header.

components.name: Buttons
components.description: Ink pill for every primary action, green with a check once added; ghost pill for the secondary action; Filters button with a green count badge.

components.name: Device Chip
components.description: Device picker pill with a status dot; pressed inverts to ink, suggested gets a green ring. On home up to three rows inside the picker bar, families on one row from 1024px, the browser guess ringed (never pressed) and named in a line whose device name is a green-underlined button: families, the family's buckets, then for a bucket that holds models a "Which model? Cases and folios fit one model only." row with the models and "Mine isn't listed"; nothing is pressed until tapped, a model re-tap steps back to its bucket and a bucket re-tap clears; elsewhere grouped by family under a muted label. On the product page the same chip is the variant picker: radio groups for Plug region, Colour, Storage and Pack under weight 600 legends, preselected on the option the SKU already is, with one muted note that options share one price.

components.name: Tags and labels
components.description: Label pills: neutral tag, hot tag in green, amber SYNTHETIC label, dashed placeholder label.
components.html: USB-CBest sellerSyntheticPlaceholder

components.name: Battery Glyph
components.description: Signature: 2.2:1 battery, 3px outline, 22px radius, green clip-path fill driven by --pct against 100W, watt figure inside. The house strip fills it to the range maximum. On a device's product page it reads the family's charge ceiling, captioned "Takes up to" over one shared ceiling sentence that says whose figure it is (the catalog's for the bucket, the bucket's for a model without its own, the model's own, or a typical figure for a catch-all) and marked indicative, on a scale stretched to the larger of 100W and the ceiling; catch-all families show none. Home's hero carries no glyph.

components.name: Split-Output Stack
components.description: Product page shared-output rows: stacked segments in the green tint ladder showing how a charger splits its output.

components.name: Product Tile
components.description: White 18px card on the grey ground: figure well, name, mini battery with watts or, with no output spec, a brand line and facet line; price, stock. Yes/no facets read as their name ("Noise cancelling" / "No noise cancelling"); prices carry thousands separators. A photo sits in the same grey well as a drawing, inset 12%, contained and multiplied so a white studio background drops into the well; the drawing hides while it is present and returns if the file is missing.

narrative.overview:
Every surface reads as a phone's lock screen in daylight while it charges. The ground is a cool near-white, the figures are near-black and set in one variable family, and a single charging green does the work of filling. Batteries fill, split-output bars fill, the pressed chip's dot fills. Nothing is decorated that is not also a reading of power.

Density is moderate and phone-first. Content sits on hairline-ruled rows and white cards on the grey ground, with pill-shaped controls that echo status chips. Depth is almost entirely tonal. The page ends with the screen asleep: one dark block, the only dark region in a light-only scheme.

The store sells devices, accessories and power, and it starts from what the shopper owns. Home opens as a retail hero in the same world: live offers, the "What do you own?" bar, and four tiles that swap from best sellers to what fits the device the shopper names. The battery stays where a figure exists: on power products it reads what a port delivers, the house strip reads the range's top output, and a device's own product page reads the ceiling the catalog lists for that device's family, marked indicative. Products with neither an output spec nor a listed ceiling carry no battery and lead with brand and facets instead.

The world uses drawn stroke icons and line-art product figures. The figures carry green port marks, and third-party devices are drawn in the same grammar with green marks, so even illustration speaks the charging language. Where the catalog has a photo, it sits in the same grey figure well as the drawing it replaces, so a photo and a drawing read as one family. The promo card's art side is the same grey well at a larger scale.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, charging green, that means "fills", "fits" and "available".
Battery glyphs as the signature component, filled with a clip-path, never a width animation.
Pills for every control and status, hairlines for every list.
Tabular figures everywhere; wattage is the headline number on power products.
Light scheme only; the footer is the screen asleep.

rules.name: The One Charge Rule
rules.body: Green means power or fit: filling, pressed, available, added. It is never used as a decorative fill, a heading color or a section background.

rules.name: The Honest Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks what is scarce or synthetic. A value that is placeholder or invented gets the amber SYNTHETIC label, never green.

rules.name: The Dormant Grey Rule
rules.body: What does not fit the chosen device is shown in grey, not hidden and not red. The scheme has no error red. A filter option that would return zero results under the current filters goes dormant the same way: grey and disabled, still listed with its zero count. An option no product in the listing carries is never offered at all. On a product page the whole reading goes dormant together: the glyph fill, the fit line and the chosen chip.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: The body sets tabular figures, so watts, prices and counts align and count-ups do not jitter.

rules.name: The Five Steps Rule
rules.body: Text sizes are 0.8, 0.875, 1, 1.25 and 1.75rem, with the tile figure stepping to 1.5rem below 720px. Larger fixed sizes are only the fluid ramps' own tops, 2.25rem and 2.75rem, used for page titles and figures. Only the display, headline and product title sizes are fluid.

rules.name: The Flat Screen Rule
rules.body: Cards, chips, tiles and category tiles never cast shadows. Hover answers with a border darkening to ink and, on tiles and linked category tiles, a 2px lift.

dos: **Do** express any level of power or fit as a fill inside a rounded track or battery, cut with clip-path and eased on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).

**Do** draw icons as 24-grid strokes at 2px with round caps, and product figures as 120-grid strokes at 3px with green ports. Third-party devices without a figure of their own are drawn the same way, with green marks at their port or face.
**Do** use pills for controls and status, hairlines for lists, and 18px cards on the grey ground.

**Do** generate gallery drawings from the catalog on a 400 by 300 grid with 3px strokes, green ports, Readex Pro labels at 12 to 15 units and 1.5 unit muted dimension lines. Draw only what the spec sheet states; a slide whose spec is missing is left out, never filled in. Thumb crops drop the labels and thicken strokes to 7 to 10 units.
**Do** label every synthetic value with the amber SYNTHETIC pill and every missing asset with the dashed placeholder pill. Never link an unbuilt page: name it in muted text and count it.
**Do** show every filter option the listing's products carry with the count it would return, and grey out options that would return nothing instead of hiding them.
**Do** show a battery only where an output or a published charge ceiling exists, and mark a device's ceiling indicative.
**Do** zero all transition and animation durations under prefers-reduced-motion.

**Do** let a chosen variant rename the product wherever it is bought (the h1, the Storage spec row, the phone buy bar, the cart line) while the page title and breadcrumb keep the SKU name, and say plainly when variants share one synthetic price.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent or use green as decoration; amber is for caution and synthetic only.
**Don't** cast shadows on cards, tiles or chips; the cart drawer, the phone filter sheet and the row scroll buttons over a row's edge are the only floating layers.
**Don't** add a dark mode or a second dark region; the footer is the screen asleep.
**Don't** fabricate product photography or borrow real brand logos; drawn line-art figures stand in until real photography exists.
**Don't** use emoji or glyph characters as icons; every icon is an inline stroke SVG.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface; Readex Pro carries display, body and figures, and the platform monospace stack is reserved for code inside notices.
